What Are Medical Billing Services?

Turning Clinical Work Into Collected Revenue

Medical billing services are the administrative and financial engine behind every visit a provider delivers. They translate a clinical encounter, such as a diagnosis, a procedure, or a note in the chart, into a properly coded claim, submit that claim to the correct payer, track it until it's adjudicated, and reconcile the payment against what was actually owed. A medical billing partner works side by side with a practice to pinpoint exactly where denials are coming from and where payments are moving too slowly, then fixes both.

Done well, medical billing is invisible to the front office and painless for patients. Done poorly, it's the single biggest source of lost revenue in a medical practice: claims sit unbilled, get rejected for formatting errors, or go unappealed after a denial and simply age out of collectability. Industry research consistently finds that a meaningful share of denied claims are never reworked at all. That is revenue a practice earned but never collects, quietly written off month after month.

Strategic billing guidance and tactical, day-to-day claim work are two different disciplines, and most practices need both. Strategy means optimizing billing processes, the technology stack, and staff skills so the whole revenue cycle improves, not just the claim in front of you. Tactical execution means making sure today's charges, today's rejections, and today's denials are actually worked before they age.

PMEX's medical billing services close that gap on both fronts with a dedicated billing team for your practice, specialty-specific coding knowledge for every claim type you generate, and a live dashboard that shows you exactly where every claim and every dollar stands, 24 hours a day.

Our Medical Billing Process

Five Stages, One Accountable Team

Every claim your practice generates moves through the same disciplined sequence. No step is skipped, and no claim is left waiting for someone to notice it stalled.

  1. 1

    Verification

    Eligibility and benefits confirmed with the payer before the visit.

  2. 2

    Charge Entry

    Encounter documentation transcribed into billable charges.

  3. 3

    Coding & Scrubbing

    ICD-10/CPT coding applied and claims scrubbed against payer edits.

  4. 4

    Submission & Tracking

    Clean claims submitted electronically and tracked to adjudication.

  5. 5

    Payment & Reconciliation

    Payments posted, balances reconciled, the provider gets paid.

This isn't a one-time workflow. It runs continuously, in parallel, across every provider and every payer your practice bills. While this week's charges move through verification and coding, last week's claims are being tracked to adjudication, and last month's denials are being appealed. Nothing waits for a slower step to catch up.

Beyond Day-to-Day Claims

Specialized Billing Support

Some billing challenges need more than claim processing. They need a strategist who understands the specific program or requirement involved.

Medicare Billing Support

Medicare billing carries its own coverage rules, documentation standards and reimbursement schedules. PMEX combines billing expertise with practice-specific revenue planning to keep Medicare claims clean and reimbursements on schedule.

Provider Enrollment Support

Joining insurance networks means navigating applications, credentialing timelines and payer contract terms. PMEX helps identify plans that benefit both the practice and its patients, and keeps enrollment moving instead of stalling in a payer queue.

Reimbursement Forms Filing

CMS 1500 and UB-04 forms require precision, and a single field error can delay a payment for weeks. PMEX manages form preparation, code auditing and timely submission so reimbursement isn't held up by paperwork.

EHR & Workflow Consultation

Switching or optimizing an EHR touches every downstream billing workflow. PMEX advises on system selection, data migration and workflow redesign so electronic billing integration goes smoothly the first time.

How We Improve Collections

Collections rarely improve from one big change. They improve when charge entry lag, claim scrubbing, denial turnaround, and A/R follow-up are all tightened at once, and kept tight, month after month.
